sources.title: Cybereason - Operation Cobalt Kitty
sources.what_it_gave: spearphishing -> Cobalt Strike, persistence, network scanning, Mimikatz credential dumping, PtH/PtT lateral movement via admin shares

sources.title: Cobalt Kitty Campaign Attack Flow (CTID corpus)
sources.what_it_gave: phish -> beacon -> discovery -> LSA secrets dump -> SMB admin shares / WMI / PtH / PtT lateral movement

narrative_before: OceanLotus (APT32) compromised an Asian corporate victim through spearphishing - both a link to a fake Flash installer delivering a Cobalt Strike beacon and Word documents with malicious macros (Cybereason). The actors established extensive persistence (scheduled tasks, Windows services, Outlook macro backdoor, registry autoruns, DLL side-loading) and used obfuscated PowerShell to run Cobalt Strike beacons. They performed network scanning and system/network discovery, dumped credentials with a modified Mimikatz (LSA secrets), and moved laterally using Net.exe over Windows admin shares (SMB), WMI, pass-the-hash and pass-the-ticket with a stolen administrative account. C2 used Cobalt Strike malleable profiles, DNS tunneling and an Outlook-based channel.

detection_moments.description: Initial access: spearphishing link/attachment delivers Cobalt Strike beacons to the victim host.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Link to a malicious site that downloads a fake Flash Installer delivering Cobalt Strike beacon ... Word documents with malicious macros downloading Cobalt Strike payloads' - CTID flow / Cybereason

detection_moments.description: Credential dumping (modified Mimikatz / LSA secrets) and lateral movement via SMB admin shares, WMI, pass-the-hash and pass-the-ticket.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Modified version of Mimikatz was used to dump credentials ... Net.exe was used to perform lateral movement via Windows Admin Shares ... pass-the-hash ... pass-the-ticket' - CTID flow / Cybereason

attack_path: Net.exe over SMB admin shares + WMI tool deployment to remote machines - T1021.002 / T1047
pass-the-hash / pass-the-ticket with stolen admin credentials - T1550.002 / T1550.003
ambiguities: Campaign-scope flow; remote lateral targets are not individually named, modelled as 3 generic hosts.
Mimikatz/credential dumping is placed on the initial victim; the flow does not attribute which specific remote host first received each lateral technique.
No defender detection timestamp; m1 = initial access, m2 = credential access + lateral movement.
